headline_stat.name: POST vs PRE significant-replay fraction (Fisher OR)

stated_limitation: The cell-identity shuffle, which permutes which cell owns which place field and is the strongest available control, comes out at about 9% rather than the nominal 5%. The per-event test is therefore liberal ... the replay result is carried by one session. Tested individually, Achilles is significant (odds ratio 2.8, p = 1e-11), Cicero is marginal (1.6, p = 0.05), and Gatsby (1.07) and Buddy (1.3) are not.

justification.dataset: DANDI:000044 CA1 linear-track recordings are the canonical dataset for sharp-wave ripples and replay, in the right species, region, and paradigm.
justification.handling: Real data streamed via remfile, correct epoch/state parsing, excitatory-unit and place-cell filtering, gap-filled speed exclusion, and defensible ripple-channel selection.
justification.analysis: Standard threshold ripple detection with six independent validation checks, Bayesian decoding with both circular-shift and time-permutation nulls, an empirical cell-ID shuffle, decoding-free EV/REV, and cross-session CMH with a homogeneity test.
justification.correctness: Headline numbers reproduce from the committed CSVs and are physically possible, but the Achilles cell-ID shuffle is reported as 8.8% in fig07/results_summary versus 6.25% in the committed multi-session CSV and fig08, a disclosed stochastic-variance inconsistency.
justification.figures: Figures are clearly labeled with units and sample sizes, show visible sharp waves, place-field tiling, and genuine posterior sweeps, and plot the empirical null alongside nominal alpha.
justification.honesty: The write-up is exceptionally calibrated: it explicitly downgrades the replay claim to a liberal per-event test, names the single-session carry, reports the homogeneity rejection, and quotes the shuffle standard error rather than overstating.
justification.verdict: The core ripple physiology is airtight and the replay analysis is rigorous and honestly bounded, so I would accept this and move on.
